9832bbfd15985289955cf7f426d6d9fb565b5c0c.summary: Insikt Group (Recorded Future) reports that RedJuliett, a likely Chinese state-sponsored group, ran cyber-espionage from November 2023 to April 2024, mainly against government, academic, technology and diplomatic targets in Taiwan. It exploited known vulnerabilities in network edge devices such as firewalls and VPNs, compromised 24 organisations, and closely overlaps with public reporting under the aliases Flax Typhoon and Ethereal Panda. The report advises network segmentation, monitoring and risk-based patching.

98db93df2c38d13d27ed23f978a9f60980941381.summary: Overview by IBM Security X-Force of ransomware seen in its 2020 incident response work. It reports rising ransom demands (over $40 million in some cases) and blended attacks that steal data before encryption. Sodinokibi (REvil) is the most frequent strain, at 29% of engagements, and ITG14 is assessed as at least one affiliate group tied to it. Manufacturing, professional services and government are the most-hit sectors. EKANS is noted for killing industrial control processes. The report recommends offline backups, multifactor authentication on remote access, and patching several listed CVEs.

It says Vidar became the most used stealer on the Russian Market from November 2025, after the takedowns of Lumma and Rhadamanthys. 98cab41503c178f8da9bd5a224ab938e28bc6726.summary: Blog post by DataBreaches (published 2023-12-18) on AlphV, also called BlackCat, claiming a breach at Viking Therapeutics. The group allegedly got an employee to file an SEC complaint under the new cyber disclosure rule, which had just taken effect that day. The post says the claim is unconfirmed, and it notes that Viking Therapeutics and the SEC did not reply to DataBreaches' inquiries. AlphV had earlier added MeridianLink to its leak site, and its SEC complaint about that victim also went nowhere.

98deb617978df37908b1ed1a79baa0e3610c360a.summary: Malpedia entry for Remcos (also called RemcosRAT), a commercial remote access tool. It is advertised as surveillance and penetration-testing software but has been used in many hacking campaigns. Once installed it opens a backdoor giving the remote user full access. The entry lists APT33, The Gorgon Group and UAC-0050 as associated actors, and a long series of vendor and researcher reports from 2017 to 2026 covering the tool, including CERT-UA reports on attacks against Ukraine.
